Catalytic Asymmetric 1,4-Hydrocarbonation of 1,3-Enynes via
Photoredox/Cobalt/Chromium Triple Catalysis
Ju-Song Yang, Xing-Yu Wang, Yong-Yao Li, Fu-Min Zhang,* Xiao-Ming Zhang, and
Yong-Qiang Tu*
Abstract: A synergistic photoredox/cobalt/chromium
triple catalysis system for regioselective, enantioselec-
tive, and diastereoselective 1,4-hydrocarbonation of
readily available 1,3-enyne precursors was explored,
providing a modular synthetic platform for various
trisubstituted axially chiral allenes bearing an extra
central chirality. The protocol features a broad substrate
scope, good functional group tolerance, excellent selec-
tivity, and mild reaction conditions. Furthermore, a
possible reaction mechanism is proposed based on
numerous control experiments and density functional
theory calculations.
Introduction
Prochiral 1,3-enynes have received extensive attention in
various asymmetric synthetic transformations using 1,4-
difunctionalization procedures because of their multiple
reaction sites and easily availability.<sup>[1–3]</sup> In particular, the
catalytic asymmetric 1,4-hydrofunctionalization of 1,3-
enynes has emerged as a method for accurately adding a
hydrogen atom and carbon or heteroatom moiety in sta-
tionary conjugate π systems.<sup>[4–9,11]</sup> Accordingly, various

copper,<sup>[6]</sup> scandium,<sup>[7]</sup> etc.) and organocatalysts<sup>[9]</sup> have been
developed to synthesize silyl-, boryl-, and aryl-substituted
axially chiral allenes via an ionic pathway (Scheme 1A, top).
However, in sharp contrast to these ionic pathways, the
radical 1,4-hydrofunctionalization of 1,3-enynes has yet to
be exploited owing to the canonical migratory insertion of
metal hydride into olefin units typically generating more
stable alkyl metal intermediates rather than dissociative
propargyl or short-lived allenic radicals.<sup>[10]</sup> To the best of
our knowledge, only one example has been reported; very
recently, Fu et al. achieved chiral nickel hydride–catalyzed
asymmetric coupling of prochiral 1,3-enynes with racemic
secondary alkyl electrophiles to simultaneously produce
central and axial chirality (Scheme 1B, bottom).<sup>[11]</sup> There-
fore, exploring new radical formation modes from 1,3-
enynes to achieve mechanistic innovations and obtain useful
multiple chiral allene architectures is urgent.
As the radical equivalent of Brønsted acid proton
transfer, TM-catalyzed (cobalt (Co), iron (Fe), manganese
(Mn), etc.) metal hydride hydrogen atom transfer (MHAT)
reactions of alkenes represent a powerful and practical
method for constructing diverse C�C and C-heteroatom
bonds.<sup>[12–18]</sup> Among them, tandem MHAT/1,2-addition was
developed by Shenvi et al. (2018)<sup>[14]</sup> and Shi et al. (2021)<sup>[15]</sup>
to couple alkyl-substituted olefins, allenes, or 1,3-dienes
with radicalophilic imines or aldehydes, respectively. For the
catalytic asymmetric version, a recent breakthrough was
elegantly disclosed by Wang et al., employing modified
photoredox/Co/chromium (Cr) triple–catalytic systems for
enantioselective 1,2-addition of benzoyloxy-substituted 1,3-
dienes to synthesize aldehydes bearing an indispensable
benzoyloxy protecting group, in which the oxygen atom in
the substrates plays an essential coordination role
(Scheme 1B).<sup>[16]</sup> Retrospectively, MHAT-meditated regio-
and chemoselective 1,4-hydrofunctionalization of more

ylate was used as an electrophile, which led to the
corresponding propargyl derivatives. To fill this gap, partic-

reacted with the chiral propargyl radical species derived

Results and Discussion
Optimization of Reaction Condition
Based on our design, we commenced catalytic asymmetric
radical–involved reductive coupling studies using
triisopropyl(pent-3-en-1-yn-1-yl)silane (1 a) and benzalde-
hyde (2 a) as the model substrates. Initially, optimization
studies were performed using cobalt tetraphenylporphine
(CoTPP, 1 mol %), chromium(II) chloride (CrCl<sub>2</sub>,
13 mol %), and photosensitizer Ir-I (1 mol %) as the triple-
catalytic metal species, our developed SPD (L1) as a chiral
ligand, Hantzsch ester (HE) as the electron and proton
donor, and tetrahydrofuran (THF) (0.05 M) as the solvent.
The reactions were performed under 70 W blue light
emitting diode irradiation for 16 h. As expected, using L1 as
the chiral ligand resulted in the desired α-allenol 3a in high
yield and good stereoselectivity (Table 1, entry 1), whereas
other nitrogen-containing ligands (L2–L9) were less effec-
tive (Table 1, entries 2–9). Subsequently, the reaction
solvents, MHAT catalyst, and other reaction parameters
were varied, respectively. Using dimethoxyethane as the
solvent caused a slight increase in yield (87 %) and stereo-
selectivity (96% ee, and >20 :1 dr) (Table 1, entry 10),
whereas chlorinated solvents such as 1,2-dichloroethane and
chlorobenzene were unsuitable for this transformation
(Table 1, entries 11 and 12, respectively). Notably, minor
inseparable propargylation regioisomers were detected
when polar dimethylformamide was used as the solvent
(Table 1, entry 13). Furthermore, the reaction hardly pro-
ceeded using iron(tetraporphyrinato) chloride (FeTPPCl) or
tetraphenylporphyrinato Mn(III) chloride (MnTPPCl) as
the MHAT catalyst instead of CoTPP (Table 1, entries 14

Conclusion
We developed a photoinduced Co/Cr dual-catalyzed 1,4-
hydrocarbonation reaction to couple prochiral 1,3-enynes
with radicalophilic aldehydes under mild, eco-friendly reac-
tion conditions, producing a series of axially chiral allenes
bearing a centrally chiral secondary alcohol unit in high
yields with excellent regioselectivity, enantioselectivity, and
diastereoselectivity. Mechanistic investigations and DFT
calculations were conducted to elucidate the origin of the
regioselectivity and stereoselectivity of this asymmetric
transformation.
